owner.occupation: Coordinator of a women's soap-making cooperative

world.bio: Coordinator of a women's soap-making cooperative in Kibera, Nairobi. Fourteen women, cold-process soap, sold at weekend markets and a few small shops. I do the books, the markets and most of the arguing with suppliers. Taking evening accounting classes, training for a 10k charity run, and my younger brother just got into university.
skills_assets: Cold-process soap making: olive, coconut and shea butter bars, goat-milk and charcoal variants
Fourteen trained members, each with a task: mixing, pouring, cutting, wrapping, selling
A rented curing room in Kibera, 4 by 6 metres, with wooden racks for about 800 bars; right now it's half empty
Weekend market stalls at Karen, Village Market and Kilimani Sunday market
Bookkeeping in a notebook plus a simple Excel sheet, M-Pesa till number
Our soaps sell fine at weekend markets but the imported lavender oil eats most of the margin

projects.name: Margin repair
projects.text: Our bar sells for KES 350, cost about KES 240, of which lavender essential oil is KES 62 per bar, imported through a supplier in Mombasa. Prices rose twice this year with the shilling and shipping costs. The curing room has space for 800 bars but we only have about 380 curing, because we can't afford to buy ingredients in bulk. I keep thinking the lavender is the problem, but I haven't looked into alternatives.

projects.name: Evening accounting course
projects.text: Tuesday and Thursday 6 to 9pm at a college in Upper Hill. Currently on cost accounting. I use the cooperative's numbers for homework, which makes my tutor happy and my group annoyed.

projects.name: Charity 10k
projects.text: Running for a girls' school fund in December. Currently at 8 km in 58 minutes. Aim: sub-60 for 10.

notes.text: Saturday market at Karen. Sold 72 bars, the best of the month. A woman bought six and said her husband used one bar in two days. 'Is it really soap or is it butter?' I laughed. I've never had a nicer complaint.

Supplier in Mombasa raised the price of lavender oil again. 15 percent. I argued on the phone for twenty minutes. He said 'sister, the shipping'. I said 'brother, my women'. We settled on 8 percent. Not a win.
Jane (member) cried today. Her son's school fees. I paid her an advance from the float. That puts our float at KES 4,300. I'll have to watch it.
Running at dawn along the Nairobi Dam. Legs heavy. A stranger shouted 'kimbia!' and I did. Not sure I enjoyed it.
Accounting class: contribution margin. My brain lit up. Our soap's contribution margin is KES 110 per bar. Without lavender it would be KES 172. I stared at that number for ten minutes.
Brother Peter called from the village: he's in university! Engineering, Kenyatta University. I screamed in the street. Mama cried on the phone. Fees: KES 38,000 a semester. We will find it.
Meeting with the women. Some want to try cheaper scents, some say customers will notice. Rose said, 'we are not selling lavender, we are selling trust.' I wrote that on the wall.
Curing room: counted 384 bars. Half empty racks look sad. Can't fill them because every shilling goes to oil and lye. I need either cheaper oil or more sales, or both.

messages.text: Said: New price lavender 8,400 per litre. Me: Last time it was 7,200. Said: Dollar. Me: I need a discount for bulk. Said: 10 litres minimum. Me: I can't afford 10.
Jane: Thank you for the advance. Me: Pay back when you can. Jane: I'll cut extra bars this week. Me: Don't overwork.
Peter: Sister, I'm worried about fees. Me: Don't. Peter: How will you manage? Me: Sell soap. Peter: Lots of soap. Me: Lots.
Organiser: Stall fee next month is going up to KES 1,800. Me: From 1,500? Organiser: Yes. Me: Please give us a month's notice next time.

calendar.event: Soap-making day, all 14 women, curing room

constraints: Every member earns at least KES 6,000 a month from the cooperative
Soap must remain natural, no synthetic fragrances
Cash float is small; no credit available from banks
sensitive: She sometimes pays members from her own savings

disclosure_policy.t0_public: Runs a women's soap cooperative in Kibera; sells at weekend markets.
disclosure_policy.t1_after_signal: Margin squeezed by imported lavender oil; curing room half empty; typical volumes and prices.
disclosure_policy.t2_after_trust: Cash float and her own savings used for members.
